mcqs.question: A common misconception is that gases have a fixed shape. Which of the following statements correctly describes the shape of a gas?

options.A: A gas takes the shape of its container.
options.B: A gas has a fixed shape like a solid.
options.C: A gas changes shape only when heated.
options.D: A gas has no shape at all, even inside a container.

mcqs.answer: A gas takes the shape of its container.
mcqs.explanation: Gases do not have a fixed shape; their particles move freely and spread out to occupy the shape of whatever container they are in. Option A states this correctly. Options B, C, and D describe incorrect ideas about gases.

mcqs.question: Why does a gas not have a fixed volume?

options.A: Because gas particles are far apart and move freely, allowing the gas to expand to fill any container.
options.B: Because gas particles are tightly packed and cannot move.
options.C: Because gas particles are attracted strongly to each other, keeping them together.
options.D: Because gas particles are solid and cannot change position.

mcqs.answer: Because gas particles are far apart and move freely, allowing the gas to expand to fill any container.
mcqs.explanation: The large distances between gas particles and their rapid, random motion let the gas expand until it occupies the entire volume available. Options B, C, and D describe properties of solids or liquids, not gases.

mcqs.question: Which statement best compares how gases and liquids behave when placed in a container of irregular shape?

options.A: Both gas and liquid take the exact shape of the container, but only the gas also fills the entire volume of the container.
options.B: Both gas and liquid have fixed shapes and do not change to fit the container.
options.C: A liquid fills the entire container, while a gas only occupies part of it.
options.D: A gas takes the shape of the container but only occupies a small portion, whereas a liquid fills the container completely.

mcqs.answer: Both gas and liquid take the exact shape of the container, but only the gas also fills the entire volume of the container.
mcqs.explanation: Liquids adopt the shape of their container but retain a definite volume, so they may not fill irregular spaces completely. Gases have neither fixed shape nor fixed volume, so they spread out to fill every part of the container. Option A captures this distinction. Options B, C, and D contain inaccurate statements about the behavior of gases and liquids.

mcqs.question: The ability of a gas to flow easily is most directly responsible for which of the following applications?

options.A: Inflating a balloon so that it expands to the shape of the balloon.
options.B: Using a gas to blow up a tire, where the gas spreads through the valve and fills the tire uniformly.
options.C: Keeping a solid ice cube solid in a freezer.
options.D: Observing the color change in a chemical reaction.

mcqs.answer: Using a gas to blow up a tire, where the gas spreads through the valve and fills the tire uniformly.
mcqs.explanation: Flowability means gas particles can move past each other and pass through narrow openings, allowing the gas to travel through a valve and occupy the tire evenly. Option B illustrates this property. Option A relates more to the gas’s ability to expand and fill space, while C and D are unrelated to gas flow.
